explanation: Truman Capote, who wrote the original novella, wanted Marilyn Monroe for the part. Hepburn's black Givenchy dress from the opening scene became a fashion icon.

claims.text: Audrey Hepburn played Holly Golightly in Breakfast at Tiffany's (1961).
Grace Kelly, Marilyn Monroe and Elizabeth Taylor did not play Holly Golightly.
Truman Capote, author of the novella Breakfast at Tiffany's, wanted Marilyn Monroe to play Holly.
Hepburn's black dress in the film's opening scene was designed by Hubert de Givenchy.

writerNotes: Self-check 9.3. Lint: clean. Claims: every claim listed, risk at or above the C26 floor; the schema's riskReason list has no only or counterintuitive, so such claims carry the nearest listed reason. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers film or TV facts, so every high-risk claim here needs checker evidence from the web. Rival test: Monroe is the lure, because Capote wanted her, but she was not cast. Kelly and Taylor were stars of the same years who never played Holly. Katharine Hepburn is left out so that two Hepburns cannot point at the key. Volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on events after mid-2026. Regional: the work is known worldwide and the options need no single country's local knowledge. Style: Oxford spelling, straight single quotes, plain hyphens, explanation of 25 words. Myths: claims screened against myths.json, no match. Mystery and encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: c3 rests on Capote's widely reported comments and should be confirmed from a reference work.
